title: Premier League Predictions: Everton and Liverpool Do Battle, Arsenal Host Man City
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-MurrayNov 26, 2026Virgil van Dijk settled the last Merseyside Derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium.  / Gareth Copley/Getty ImagesThe Premier League delivered high-quality drama last weekend as Mauricio Pochettino was pummelled on his Manchester United debut by Liverpool, Chelsea were thrashed on their own patch and each of the division’s top three sides, including Arsenal and Manchester City, dropped points.
Whether Gameweek 12 can provide similar entertainment remains to be seen, but an intriguing fixture list certainly could facilitate yet more chaos.

The biggest matches of the round bookend Sunday’s action, with the Merseyside derby between Everton and Liverpool kicking things off and Arsenal vs. Manchester City closing the show. The weekend began with some fireworks as Nottingham Forest piled the pressure on Xabi Alonso and Chelsea by romping to a raucous 3–2 victory on Friday night.
With that in mind, here are Sports Illustrated’s score predictions for the upcoming Premier League gameweek.

After beating Tottenham Hotspur and annihilating Chelsea in their last two matches, Leeds have restored the feel-good factor around Elland Road. They had endured a couple of blips prior to successive victories, but begin the weekend seventh in the table after an overwhelmingly impressive start to the campaign.

Noah Okafor has joined the party over recent matches, scoring three times in his last two games, and will once again support the clinical Dominic Calvert-Lewin in attack against Coventry City. On paper, the Whites should have too much in the tank for their guests, especially considering they boast the joint second-best defensive record in the league.

Coventry have shot up to 14th after winning two of their last three, but their away form appears set to be an issue. They have lost four of their five games on the road, conceding 10 times and scoring just three in the process.
Man Utd are chasing their first win under Mauricio Pochettino. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesPrediction: Man Utd 2–1 Brentford

Good fortune has eluded Mauricio Pochettino at the beginning of his Manchester United reign, with pivotal decisions going against him and his players in the humbling 4–0 loss to Liverpool and frenzied 2–2 draw with Sporting CP midweek. Perhaps Lady Luck will finally pay him a visit at Old Trafford this weekend.

United host Brentford in desperate need of points to exit the relegation zone, with just one win to their name from 11 Premier League outings. Their sole triumph did come on home turf back in Gameweek 2, as they secured an emphatic 5–2 victory over Ipswich Town.

There were some positive signs during the stalemate in Lisbon on Wednesday night, and the Old Trafford faithful should act as United’s 12th man this Saturday for Pochettino’s home debut. A magical performance from the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha would be timely.

Brentford are no pushovers, though, and are nine points better off than the Red Devils for good reason. Keith Andrews’s organized outfit regularly secure major scalps, as United know all too well having suffered defeats in two of their last three games against the Bees—although they have won all five games played at Old Trafford this decade.

There are just three matches staged across a lightly-packed Saturday schedule, with Aston Villa traveling to Ipswich Town during the late kickoff. While not the most glamorous occasion, there could be plenty of entertainment to enjoy at Portman Road.

Ipswich have been involved in some high-scoring affairs this season, including two seperate 3–2 scorelines already, and have picked up seven of their 11 points on home soil. They have only been beaten twice in Suffolk in the league, losing to Liverpool and Bournemouth.

Aston Villa have been at the center of some thrillers themselves, albeit not their most recent goalless draw with Sunderland. Their last Premier League away day saw eight goals equally shared between themselves and Man Utd in a fixture which showcased both the best and worst of Unai Emery’s side.
Liverpool have won their last three ahead of the Merseyside derby. / NICOLAS TUCAT/AFP/Getty ImagesPrediction: Everton 1–1 Liverpool

The first Merseyside derby of the season and Andoni Iraola’s tenure arrives in Sunday’s earliest encounter, with in-form Liverpool making the brief trip to the Hill Dickinson Stadium—where they have a perfect record after last season’s last-gasp victory.

Traditionally, however, the Reds have struggled away from Anfield against their neighbors, only winning two of the last nine visits to Everton. Six of those matches have finished in draws, an incredibly common outcome for this fixture in the Premier League era.

Everton come into the fixture off the back of a bruising 4–0 defeat to Brentford, during which James Tarkowski was sent off. The influential defender will be suspended for the visit of Liverpool, who have won their last three games by scoring three or more times in each triumph.
